findings.issue: The test makes an unnecessary successful `Ledger.submit` call after commit before touching the child. That `submit` advances the task state and depends on submission bookkeeping unrelated to `worktree_digest`. The test could remove it. It should only assert that the post-commit digest equals the snapshot, change the child, and assert the submit fails. This is a scope/minimality defect, not a digest-correctness defect.

I could not run tests in this review (file-tools only; coordinator executes the gate). The root-cause analysis matches the code: before this change, `path.exists()` was false for a tracked path replaced by a directory, so the path name was skipped, while after commit the nested child file was indexed and hashed. The fix skips any non-symlink directory. The stated stable properties (deletion, rename, directory replacement, symlink-target change detection, coordinator sub-file edit detection) follow by inspection checkpoint, but runtime execution is unverified here.

checks: Inspected scripts/agy_runner.py worktree_digest lines 20-43: new guard `if not path.is_symlink() and (not path.exists() or path.is_dir()): continue` skips only non-symlink directory paths; symlinks (including dangling/dir-target) remain hashed via os.readlink; regular files hash exec bit + sha256; other existing non-regular entries hash b'missing' — unchanged from prior behavior except directory skip.

Verified the directory-vs-index inconsistency is real: git workout `ls-files --cached --others` lists `docs/start.md` before commit (tracked) and, after the model replaces the file with a directory containing `nested/child.md`, post-commit index no longer lists `docs/start.md` so only leaf files are hashed; prior code would have included the tracked file name and not the nested child because `path.exists()` is False for a directory inside `worktree/.../docs/start.md` — confirming the pre/post divergence the probe detects.

Confirmed symlink semantics preserved: Path.is_symlink() short-circuits the directory check, so any symlink (dangling, pointing at a directory料酒) still contributes its raw readlink target; execute() snapshots post-run and submit compares to recorded worktree_digest (submit fails on mismatch).

Read test_directory_replacement...: FAKE_AGY=directory fixture unlinks docs/start.md, creates docs/start.md/nested/child.md; asserts success, digest equality, digest stable post `git add -A`, stable post commit, submit reaches review, then child content edit changes digest and submit raises snapshot Error after coordinating commit.

Read test_symlink...: cases start.md (link-target -> .), file-link.md (link-target/one.md -> link-target/two.md), dangling-link.md (absent-one -> absent-two) each retarget and assert digest changes even when targets are dirs/same-content/dangling, restore and assert digest equal; then retarget start.md to '.' and commit and assert submit raises snapshot Error. Good coverage of non-following/raw-target hashing.

Read test_original_directory_replacement_probe_is_stable: calls evolution.snapshot_probe(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]) and asserts result['stable']; snapshot_probe imports scripts path (agy_runner) in a child python and runs git init/add/commit inside a TemporaryDirectory with clean GIT_ env; confirms original discovery probe passes and becomes a permanent regression.

Doc diff docs/subsystems/coordination.md lines 58-62 adds Chinese text matching implementation: snapshot covers Git-visible paths/content/exec bit/symlink target, does not follow links (dangling/dir-target counted), ignores index-listed paths deleted or replaced by real directories in worktree while validating Git-visible files/links inside, so delete/rename/file->directory consistent pre/post stage+commit; coordinator edits of child files or link targets still fail submit.
